haiku-low.q1: Reads reports.row_count. At 10,000 or fewer, the CSV is the click's response. Above that, a background job runs and emails a 24-hour download link.
haiku-low.q2: The second click gets the first export back with 202, not a new one. A stale queued or running export is taken over instead.
haiku-low.q3: The link works 24 hours (86,400 s). The bucket's 7-day lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation. No code deletes files.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, retried after 60 s and 300 s. Then the row is marked failed and the user gets a failure email.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica only, never the primary.
haiku-low.q6: In the exports table on the primary. The page polls GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running, and fetches it again on reopen.
haiku-low.q7: Reads 5,000-row keyset pages, buffering 8 MiB parts uploaded with upload_part. Only part etags stay in memory; the file appears only at completion.
haiku-low.q8: Parts stay in an unfinished upload. The next attempt aborts it and restarts from the first row, since no progress is saved.
haiku-low.q9: Copied into the exports row as filters and cols. The job gets only export_id and reads the view from that row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The losing insert reads the winning row.
haiku-low.q11: A complete file: status done with file_key set after complete_multipart. A rerun on a done export skips the build and goes to the email step.
haiku-low.q12: Before the first byte: JSON 500. After streaming starts: the connection breaks, the fetch fails, the page saves no partial file, and the user can retry.

sonnet.q1: Chosen by reports.row_count (unfiltered total): 10,000 or fewer uses the small path, above uses the job. Small path: the response to the click is the CSV itself (text/csv, attachment, header row first), nothing stored. Large path: 202 with the export's state, a background job writes the file to object storage, the page shows progress, and the user is emailed a download link.
sonnet.q2: A second click returns the first export (202), not a new one, unless the existing one is stale (queued with no job id >5 min, or running with no heartbeat >60 min). A stale one is marked failed with error 'abandoned' and a new export is created. Different filters on the second click still return the first export; the page shows that export's filters.
sonnet.q3: The signed link works 24 hours (86,400 s). The file is removed by the bucket's lifecycle rule 7 days after creation; no code deletes files.
sonnet.q4: 3 attempts in total (retries after 60 s, then 300 s). After attempt 3 fails, on_final_failure aborts any upload, sets the row failed with error 'build failed after 3 attempts', and sends the failed email (a link to the report page to start again, no internal details). The page shows the error text and a Try again button. (If the row was already done, it stays done and the ready email is resent instead.)
sonnet.q5: The read replica (never the primary) for report rows. Export state is on the primary. Whether reports.row_count is readable from the replica is an unconfirmed item.
sonnet.q6: In the exports table on the primary database (status, attempt, rows_written, heartbeat_at, etc.). The page calls GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/latest when it loads, and polls it every 5 seconds while the export is queued or running (backing off up to 30 s if the endpoint fails). It stops polling at done or failed. On reopening, the page load calls the same endpoint, which returns the caller's most recent export, so the state comes from the server.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads rows in pages of 5,000 via keyset paging and buffers up to 8 MiB, then uploads each as a multipart part, keeping only the etags in memory. Memory is one 8 MiB part plus one page of rows plus a few MB of overhead, far below 512 MB. The final complete_multipart makes the file visible.
sonnet.q8: Parts already uploaded stay in an unfinished multipart upload, and nothing is visible at the file key, so a half-written file can't be downloaded. The next attempt aborts the old upload (abort_multipart, ignoring not-found) and starts again from the beginning (new upload, header row, first row), because the queue saves no progress. The bucket also discards unfinished uploads after 24 hours. If failure happens after the row is marked done, the next attempt only resends the email.
sonnet.q9: They are copied from the click request into the filters and cols columns of the new exports row (on the primary). The job payload is only {"export_id": ...}, and the job reads filters and cols from that row.
sonnet.q10: A partial unique index on exports (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The losing insert fails on the index, and that request reads the winning row and returns it with 202.
sonnet.q11: Before the email: the multipart upload has been completed (file visible at its key), the row is marked done with file_key and completed_at (only if attempt matches and status is running), then a signed URL is made and the ready email is sent, setting email_sent_at on success. If the job runs again: the claim exits without work if no row matches (stale or duplicate); if the row is already done, the done check skips straight to resending the email (item i) and exits, with no new file.
sonnet.q12: If the error comes before the first byte, a JSON 500 is returned. If it comes after streaming starts, or the 60-second cutoff hits, the connection breaks, the page's fetch fails so it doesn't save the partial file, and the user sees an error and can try again. Nothing was stored.
